types.name: Note
types.label: note
types.summary: Teaching text with example sentences (has audio). Not scored.
types.description: Explains a point in a few short paragraphs, with example sentences the learner can tap to hear. Open a lesson with one, or put one before each new idea.
types.checking: Not scored — the learner reads and continues.

types.name: Word order
types.label: word order
types.summary: Arrange tiles into the correct sentence.
types.description: The sentence is cut into tiles (words or phrases) in a shuffled order; the learner taps them into the right order. The English is hidden until asked for, so the Chinese does the work.
types.checking: Automatic — the tile order must match (alternative orders can be accepted).

types.name: Multiple choice
types.label: multiple choice
types.summary: Pick the sentence or word that fits (2–5 options).
types.description: A situation or question with 2–5 Chinese options. Pinyin and English appear only after answering, with your explanation.

types.name: Translate
types.label: translate
types.summary: English → Chinese, self-checked against a reference.
types.description: The learner translates an English sentence into Chinese (typed, or in their head), then compares with your reference answer.
types.checking: Self-assessed — an exact match is highlighted, other wordings can still be right.

types.name: Match pairs
types.label: match pairs
types.summary: Connect Chinese words with their meanings (2–8 pairs).
types.description: Two shuffled columns — Chinese and English — to connect. Quick vocabulary warm-up.
types.checking: Automatic — correct when every pair is matched without a wrong tap.

types.name: Describe picture
types.label: describe picture
types.summary: An illustration is generated; the learner describes it aloud.
types.description: An illustration is generated from your scene description; the learner describes it out loud, then sees your reference description.

types.name: Speak
types.label: speak
types.summary: Say your own sentence out loud, self-assessed.
types.description: A quick speaking prompt ("Order two coffees, one iced."). Nothing is recorded — use Oral expression when you want to hear the answer.
types.checking: Self-assessed, optionally against an example answer.

types.name: Listen & pick
types.label: listen & pick
types.summary: Audio plays with text hidden; pick what you heard (tones, minimal pairs).
types.description: A sentence is played with the text hidden; the learner picks what they heard. Built for tones and minimal pairs (有 yǒu vs 又 yòu).

types.name: Listen & translate
types.label: listen & translate
types.summary: Audio plays hidden; translate what you heard.
types.description: A sentence is played with the text hidden; the learner says or types what it means, then sees the transcript and translation.

types.name: Sentence making
types.label: sentence making
types.summary: Make your own sentence with the target words — typed or handwritten.
types.description: The learner writes their OWN sentence using 1–4 target words, optionally in a situation you set. Choose typed or handwritten input. Online, Claude checks the sentence and suggests a correction; offline the learner compares with your example.
types.checking: Claude feedback when online (grammar, naturalness, were the words used); self-assessed offline.

types.name: Writing — typed
types.label: typed writing
types.summary: Type the characters from the meaning / pinyin (choosing the right characters).
types.description: Shows the English and/or pinyin (or plays it) and the learner types the characters with their keyboard — practising picking the right characters for the sounds.
types.checking: Automatic — punctuation and spaces ignored; wrong characters are highlighted.

types.name: Writing — handwriting
types.label: handwriting
types.summary: Write the characters by hand on the writing pad (≤ 12 characters).
types.description: Shows the English and/or pinyin and the learner writes the characters by hand from memory, one character per square, on the stroke-order writing pad. Keep it to a word or short phrase.
types.checking: The writing pad checks every stroke — order, direction, shape — and hints after misses; right when written from memory. You see each stroke they drew. (Self-assessed if the stroke data isn’t on the device yet.)

types.name: Dictation
types.label: dictation
types.summary: Hear a sentence and write down what you heard — typed or handwritten.
types.description: A sentence is played with the text hidden; the learner writes down exactly what they heard. Choose typed input (checked character by character) or handwriting.
types.checking: Typed: automatic, character by character. Handwritten: the writing pad checks every stroke (characters hidden).

types.name: Oral expression
types.label: oral expression
types.summary: Answer a prompt out loud — the answer is recorded for you to hear.
types.description: A speaking prompt (optionally a question played in Chinese, with useful words). The learner records their answer, can play it back, then compares with your model answer. You can listen to the recording afterwards; it is transcribed when online.

types.name: Conversation
types.label: conversation
types.summary: A dialogue in two voices; listen, then answer comprehension questions.
types.description: A dialogue between two people in a situation (booking a hotel, ordering food, at the doctor…) played with a different voice for each speaker and the text hidden. The learner listens (and replays) the whole conversation, then answers questions about what happened. The transcript with pinyin and English is revealed at the end.
types.checking: Multiple-choice questions automatic; free answers self-assessed. One point per question.

exercises.title: Doing something TO something
exercises.body:
把 moves the object in front of the verb: Subject + 把 + object + verb + result.

Use it when you do something to a specific thing and something happens to it — it gets finished, moved, closed.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ zuòyè zuò wán le.

exercises.question: You want a friend at dinner to pass you the salt. You say:

options.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yán dì gěi wǒ.
Qǐng yán bǎ dì gěi wǒ.

exercises.explanation: 把 + the object comes before the verb 递给 (pass to).

exercises.english: Please put the book on the table.
exercises.reference_pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shū fàng zài zhuōzi shang.

exercises.image_prompt: A small café counter: a barista hands two cups of coffee to a smiling woman, a chalkboard menu behind them, warm morning light
exercises.reference_hanzi: 服务员给一位女士两杯咖啡。
exercises.reference_pinyin: Fúwùyuán gěi yí wèi nǚshì liǎng bēi kāfēi.
exercises.reference_english: The waiter gives a woman two cups of coffee.

exercises.prompt: Order two coffees, one of them iced.

example.hanzi: 我要两杯咖啡，一杯冰的。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yào liǎng bēi kāfēi, yì bēi bīng de.
example.english: I’d like two coffees, one iced.

audio.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi zhè běn shū.
audio.english: I want to buy this book.

exercises.question: Which verb did you hear?
exercises.explanation: 买 mǎi (third tone, dips) = buy; 卖 mài (fourth tone, falls) = sell.

exercises.task: Explain why you were late today.

example.hanzi: 因为路上堵车，所以我迟到了。
example.pinyin: Yīnwèi lùshang dǔchē, suǒyǐ wǒ chídào le.
example.english: Because there was traffic, I was late.

exercises.task: A friend invites you to lunch — tell them you have already eaten.

answer.english: I’m going to the hospital tomorrow.

audio.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng.
audio.english: He gets up at seven every morning.

audio.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài guì le.
audio.english: This piece of clothing is too expensive.

exercises.prompt: Talk about what you did last weekend — where you went and who with.

question_audio.pinyin: Nǐ shàng ge zhōumò zuòle shénme?
question_audio.english: What did you do last weekend?

example.hanzi: 上个周末我和朋友去了公园，我们在那儿吃了午饭。
example.pinyin: Shàng ge zhōumò wǒ hé péngyou qùle gōngyuán, wǒmen zài nàr chīle wǔfàn.
example.english: Last weekend I went to the park with friends; we had lunch there.

spec.title: Checking in at a hotel
spec.description: A conversation lesson: set the scene, listen to the dialogue in two voices, then the phrases and your turn.

exercises.body: You’re checking in at a hotel front desk in Beijing. Two words you’ll hear:

exercises.situation: Checking in at a hotel front desk

lines.hanzi: 您好！欢迎光临。请问有预订吗？
lines.pinyin: Nín hǎo! Huānyíng guānglín. Qǐngwèn yǒu yùdìng ma?
lines.english: Hello, welcome! Do you have a reservation?

lines.hanzi: 有，我叫王明，订了一个双人间。
lines.pinyin: Yǒu, wǒ jiào Wáng Míng, dìngle yí ge shuāngrénjiān.
lines.english: Yes, my name is Wang Ming. I booked a double room.

lines.hanzi: 好的，请给我看一下您的护照。
lines.pinyin: Hǎo de, qǐng gěi wǒ kàn yíxià nín de hùzhào.
lines.english: OK, may I see your passport, please?

lines.pinyin: Gěi nín. Wǒ zhù sān ge wǎnshang.
lines.english: Here you are. I’m staying three nights.

lines.hanzi: 您的房间是八零六，在八楼。早饭七点到十点。
lines.pinyin: Nín de fángjiān shì bā líng liù, zài bā lóu. Zǎofàn qī diǎn dào shí diǎn.
lines.english: Your room is 806, on the eighth floor. Breakfast is from seven to ten.

lines.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ yǒu wúxiàn wǎng ma?
lines.english: Is there Wi-Fi in the room?

lines.hanzi: 有，密码在房卡上。祝您住得愉快！
lines.pinyin: Yǒu, mìmǎ zài fángkǎ shang. Zhù nín zhù de yúkuài!
lines.english: Yes, the password is on your key card. Enjoy your stay!

questions.question: How many nights is the guest staying?
Which floor is the room on?
questions.explanation: 八零六，在八楼 — room 806, on the 8th floor.

exercises.body: Three phrases from the front desk worth keeping.

exercises.prompt: You are the guest. Check in: give your name, how many nights you are staying, and ask one question about the hotel.

example.hanzi: 你好，我叫王明，有预订。我住两个晚上。请问早饭几点？
example.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ jiào Wáng Míng, yǒu yùdìng. Wǒ zhù liǎng ge wǎnshang. Qǐngwèn zǎofàn jǐ diǎn?
example.english: Hi, I’m Wang Ming, I have a reservation. I’m staying two nights. What time is breakfast?
